mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as lower rates reduce the cost of capital and increase equity valuation multiples.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in < 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 2.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.3% signals inflationary pressure that leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as central banks may tighten policy.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in < 40% of triggered instances despite CPIAUCSL monthly change > 0.3%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A strong labor market, indicated by unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% and positive monthly employment growth (PAYEMS > 0.5% monthly), supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as it reflects robust economic activity and corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in < 40% of triggered instances despite UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS monthly growth > 0.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (defined by GDP growth above 3.0% annualized and unemployment below 4.0%), a high CPI (CPIAUCSL) signals inflationary pressures that lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as central banks may preemptively tighten policy.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in < 40% of instances where GDPC1 > 3.0% annualized, UNRATE < 4.0%, and CPIAUCSL > 2.5% (annualized), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
